summary.name: Ravenpass
summary.one_liner: Ravenpass is an open-source, local-first password and secrets manager for macOS and Android that stores passwords, passkeys, two-factor codes, cards, identities and notes in an encrypted vault file.
use_cases: Store passwords and passkeys on a Mac and Android phone
Generate and read two-factor codes next to logins
Keep card numbers and billing details for autofill
Sync an encrypted vault between devices via a cloud folder
Back up and verify crypto wallet recovery phrases
Import passwords exported from another password manager
summary.what_it_does: Ravenpass stores logins, passkeys, two-factor codes, payment cards, identities, private notes and recovery phrases in an encrypted vault file. The vault can be kept on the local device or in a cloud folder the user chooses, and the page says there is no account, no telemetry and the project is open source. It autofills logins in apps and browsers on macOS and Android, with a Chrome extension that requires the desktop app. Unlock is available with fingerprint, screen lock or PIN. It can import passwords from other managers and offers automatic encrypted backups plus a 24-word recovery key.
notable: Local-first encrypted vault file with optional cloud folder sync, no account required
Stores two-factor codes and passkeys alongside the sign-in they belong to
Wallet seed storage with checksum validation and a way to test written backups
Card entries shown with the bank's logo
caveats: Beta software; the page advises keeping a backup of stored items
Windows, Linux and iOS are not yet available
Requires macOS 13+ (Apple silicon) and Android 12+; Chrome extension needs Chrome 133+ and the desktop app
Lost vault file cannot be restored from the recovery key and nobody can reset the vault
